name: Bitwarden
summary: Bitwarden has a free organization for two users, a Teams plan at $4 per user a month and an Enterprise plan at $6, both billed annually. Its code is public on GitHub, and Enterprise customers can run the server on their own infrastructure.

facts.text: Bitwarden publishes its full codebase on GitHub under the AGPL v3.0 or the Bitwarden License.
Bitwarden lists yearly third-party audits by firms including Cure53, Fracture Labs and Mandiant, plus a 2025 review by the Applied Cryptography Group at ETH Zurich.
Organizations on the Enterprise plan can host the Bitwarden server themselves.

Bitwarden reported that a malicious version of its command-line tool, @bitwarden/cli 2026.4.0, was available on npm for a short window on April 22, 2026, and said it had found no evidence that vault data was accessed.
Bitwarden states it is working toward FedRAMP authorization and is not yet authorized.

plans.name: Free organization
plans.notes: Up to 2 users and 2 collections, without policies or event logs

hiddenCosts: Login with single sign-on, enterprise policies and self-hosting are on the Enterprise plan only.
Secrets Manager is priced separately at $6 per user a month with Teams and $12 with Enterprise.

contract.cancellation: Refunds are available only for subscriptions less than 30 days old; after cancellation the organization stays active until the next charge date.
contract.dataExport: Plain JSON, plain CSV or encrypted JSON, by admins and owners.
